prompt: Reference image 1 shows the chosen design of Ending "The Flagship Slips Away". Keep the referenced design exactly and show it in this new composition: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, limited saturated palette, widescreen arcade composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; ending scene painted at hi-resolution, minimal and enormous, ultra-detailed large-format art with pixel-texture accents. Almost nothing, said at maximum scale: a totally flat, empty post-storm ocean under a low slate-and-cream cloud ceiling at grey dawn, the horizon dead straight and splitting the frame exactly in two, sea-line rimmed in pale silver. On the water's face there is no ship above it — until you look down. Beneath the surface, the water itself is holding the shape of what just passed: a faint, vast, slow-fading silhouette of an ark diving at a shallow angle into the depths, suggested only by a broad smudge of deeper blue, a scattering of silver bubbles trailing off its tail end toward nothing, and along the length of its descending back a single diminishing line of cold teal porthole-glow — a string of lamps going out one by one from front to back as the deep claims the last of them. The highest, last-glowing lamp is still a small hard star under the water, the deepest is already invisible. The upper half of the frame, the whole empty world of air and cloud, does not react to this at all. Nothing else exists in the image: no land, no birds, no foreground fighter. The painting is the difference between a surface that looks peaceful and a depth that knows. Palette of slate blue, pearl grey, dawn cream, and one thinning thread of teal light under the water, lifted deep-navy shadows, never pure black. No text, no letters, no UI. No text anywhere.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, whale visible, ship on surface, boats, island, birds, sun rays, storm, big waves, glowing monster clear, neon water, text, watermark, blurry, cluttered composition, horizon off-center
